9502.d:
"It's not true, but I believe it!": I am always surprised by that trait of human nature that makes people prefer to believe what best makes them feel good even if obviously false, be it a confirmation, a justification, a reassuring or a pleasant belief. Although the scientific method is an example of a remedy, scientific knowledge has often been shown to suffer from this epistemological problem.

Probably this behaviour gives some evolutionistic advantage, expecially to restricted groups of sapiens very busy in the harsh and boring task of fulfilling their stomaches every day. Are art, religion, politics and second hand cars a desirable effect of this? 

"Victorian Turbation Set" generates table legs via a simple algorithm, a set of original textures and the 3D representation power of Threejs. No interactivity provided to leave your hands completely free. Watch it fulscreen for the best turbation.

Being a conceptual work I had no interest in complicating too much the design with style variations and accurate fidelity to the designs I've found in documentation phase.

Drawing from from The Strand Magazine, No. 30, 1893, public domain

9505.d:
This work is the result of composition and division of triangles.

The background layer consists of a grid of 4 or 6 point polygons that are composed of triangles.
On top, there are an outer, middle and inner object, each again a composition of triangles with a randomized number of points.

Each triangle on its own is divided into pieces using a randomized number of iterations,

Chaikin curved lines are used to create the floral effect.

For the background layer, the palette colours are used (see features), the other layers use random colours.

The style of this piece can be considered as generative geometric art. Each mint is the result of math, no design has been done to manipulate the outcome.

Controls:
* Press "s" to save the current image

Features:
- palette: 33 possible variations of sets of 4 colours
- # of points in background layer
- # of points in middle layer
- # of points in inner layer
- # of iterations for background objects
- # of iterations for outer objects
- # of iterations for middle objects
- # of iterations for inner objects

Made in Zoutleeuw, Belgium by Gorik with p5

CHOOSE YOUR OWN ADVENTURE - Hash Nos is a collection of:
*A) Digital abstract works, each of which also features a nose.
*B) Nose-based PFPs, each of which also features various abstract shapes.

Whichever adventure you choose, there are many possibilities. Each piece in the Hash Nos series will be generated by drawing upon 481 unique PNG elements. Each of these elements is pre-made and has been organised unevenly across 36 different layers.

When a piece is generated, it will take one element from each of these 36 layers. There is an equal probability for each of the PNG elements across 35 of these layers. The final layer, however, is where the magic happens. It is in this layer that the nose elements are located.

In the final layer you will be rewarded with either a: Rainbow(1), Gold(2), Red(5), Green(10), Pink(15), Blue(20) or Grey(30) nose. The number after each of the nose colors above, is the likelihood of receiving one. For example: A chance of 5 (Red nose) is half as likely to appear as a chance of 10 (Green Nose), but five times as likely as a chance of 1 (Rainbow Nose). Basically, the lower the number, the rarer your nose. Rainbow noses are the most rare, Grey noses are the least.

Creator Notes: 
* Hash Nos is a companion series to ‘Hoc Nos’, a collection by Luke Conroy on OBJKT.com
* Each possible PNG element is a 100% original creation of the artist. The code used to make these elements come together, is by the genius and generous @PureSpider.
* CC BY-NC-ND 4.0

9519.d:
Flow is a collection of animations based on noise fields and fluid dynamics. The pieces are designed to run continuously, and they produce slowly evolving images that seem to drip, swirl, pulse, and flow. Dense networks of patterns emerge and decay as the pieces evolve. Because of their subtle movement, these pieces make excellent wall art when run on a display monitor.

The algorithm is sensitive to canvas size and will animate differently depending on the size of the window in which it is running. Optimal viewing size is at a resolution of at least 1,000 x 1,000 pixels, while smaller animations will tend to flow faster, develop fewer eddies, and build more simplistic patterns. In this way, each iteration represents not just a single animation, but a large number of closely related animations that can be explored. To see the exact same animation, you must run it at the exact same size. 

-spacebar will pause the animation

-return will resume the animation

-r will restart the animation

-s will allow you to save a still capture

There are 24 color palettes, all equal in rarity. These other features have some variations that are more common than others:

Background Color
Irregularity
Attractor Density
Falloff

Flow, 2022
-hieroglyphica

9542.d:
Vanilla JS + SVG
January 2022

Edition of 512

"Off the grid" is my attempt to bring human imperfection to the strict formality of a generative grid-based piece.

Grid-plotted geometric forms are very slightly offset, rotated out of position by a degree or two, or absented entirely from the grid. The number of passes is dictated by the hash, and the results will vary from minimal (4 passes) to maximal (13 passes). The sizes of the forms can vary or be all the same, leading to quite different outputs, further emphasized by the different 'canvas' sizes.

The features are:
Format (Portrait, Landscape or Square), Palette (10 in total), Coverage (Full or Indented), Passes (the number of times the algorithm makes a grid) and Sizes (the sizes of the shapes in the grid, Single [one size] or Multiple).

'S' saves an SVG
'P' saves a PNG

[Please note this project will display, but will not work as intended on most IOS devices]

Rugby is a modern interpretation of classic oriental rugs, which are conceived using generative design methods and antique-driven designs that can adapt and morph. The patterns are based on traditional nomadic designs from Persia, Anatolia, Armenia, Central Asia, and southern Russia.

The generative process of Rugby creates unlimited possibilities for unique and intricate rug designs. Each rug is unique and the constellation of motifs changes with each design. The patterns vary from one corner to the other. Some of the designs may appear at first as if they were quadruply mirrored, but they are not. The motifs never repeat themselves and thus, even after decades of possession and viewing, one can always find new details.

Love, Kyraian.

Avocados consists of 3 agents running in the foreground and a number of other agents running in the background.

Each agent operates independently from the rest, updating their position based on their current angle and speed. Each step, they also adjust their angle based on a custom trigonometric function.

There are a number of different variables input variables that affect how the agents update their angle over time. Though these variables will vary from one NFT to the next, within a single image, agents will share all of those inputs except for one.

Features:
Initial alignment of background agents: random, horizontal, vertical, origin
Which variable agents modify: sin, cos, curviness, initialAngle, speed

Keyboard:
Press 'a' to view the generation of the image as an animation
Press 'f' to toggle back to the finalized version

A “Puppeteer” consists of one or two abstract animated hands with fingers which are controlled by strings from above as well as exercise control via strings over something below. It is quite mesmerizing and a little bit creepy to watch the hands float around constrained by their strings. In some variations they almost seem to dance.

The hands and fingers are placed and sized randomly with some constraints. The initial segment lengths of a finger are arranged in the “golden ratio”. Each joint has a unique movement pattern and thus influencing the attached finger segments and strings.

Features and variations include are "Background color", "Accent color palette", "Is controlled", "Controls others", "Controlled by color", "Controls with color", "Has left hand", "Has right hand", "Fingers per hand"

Some variations are more common than others.

The most common variation would be a two handed “Puppeteer” with five fingers per hand on dark background with neon color palette and strings above and below.

The other extreme in terms of rarity would be a one handed “Puppeteer” with 2 or 6 fingers on light background with grey color palette and no strings attached.

Extra:
- Press “p” to pause/play animation
- Press “s” to grab a still of current frame
- Press “w” to record and download a 5 second .webm video clip from current frame
- Press “e” to record and download a 10 second .webm video clip from current frame

Created with JavaScript on canvas.

This work is an artistic investigation into the visual weight of colors and based on preliminary research results: Each piece is based on an analogous color harmony and displays a range of hues arranged around a single primary color, while the balancing algorithm varies the forms and the area coverage of the color fields and their respective brightness to keep the whole composition in visual balance.

In terms of color scheme, typography and design, the work is inspired by the International Typographic Style movement (Swiss Style), which was characterized by clarity, openness, a desire for democracy, a highly intellectual approach and the credo that design - and the designer himself - should take a "backseat" in the creation and even become "invisible". All of this, I believe, is also a very fitting description of the generative art scene.

The primary color in each piece is denoted by one out of 24 different color tables (some rarer than others), which cover the full 360° degree range of hues. Furthermore, there are three different grid sizes (3x3, 4x4 and 5x5), two positions for the typography (top and bottom) and four different paper stocks (coated cool white, uncoated cool while, uncoated warm white and newspaper).

The token is rendered in high resolution (4800x6000px) in the background, which allows for saving and printing in high quality up to a height of about 20" (50cm).

(Accalance 2 allows for interactions both with the keyboard and with the mouse wheel. See the description of the collected pieces for details.)

A cognitive map is a spatio-temporal representation of the outside world kept within the mind. Cognitive maps also underlie our ability to generalize and make inferences.

The neural basis of cognitive maps was speculated to be within grid and place cells of the brain.

The cells were called “grid cells” because they have multiple excitation areas, the geometric position of which had the symmetry of a hexagonal lattice. 

Together, place cells and grid cells create a virtual coordinate system to determine the spatial position, direction, and speed of movement at a particular point in time. 

Therefore I believe that the cognitive maps are the physiological representation of the space-time continuum 

This art takes the neuronal hexagonal spatial lattice and attempts to visualize it using a simple monochrome palette; pulsations are representative of temporal neuronal firing. 

By @trp_chai 

February 19 2022 

Made with p5.js

9607.d:
‘There is a Clock at the Heart of the Universe’ is an exercise in restrained rotation. At its simplest, a line is extended and rotated around a point, varying graphical effects added along its length, for a fixed number of frames. The angle at which the line rotates is increased slightly over time, though the underlying rotation value ensures it completes at least one full rotation. Colours, stroke weight and translucency are affected by time and distance, producing radial effects like the spokes of a wheel.

There are seven render modes in There is a Clock at the Heart of the Universe, with varied levels of rarity. Two of the modes feature thin, translucent lines, and thus produce lighter pieces: to compensate for this, when this render mode is activated the required number of frames is also increased. Other renders produce darker outputs, with solid-outlines and, in once case, a coloured fill; these are also tweaked to produce viable output. Custom parameters for different render modes, carefully adjusted, help the piece to realise its potential for variance and interest.

The render modes work on a smaller scale, adding tiny detail to a 2048x2048 canvas. On top of this, larger detail is added in the form of circles, often equally-spaced, and relatively bold additions to the canvas. You may spot light or dark flashes as these are added to the canvas during the rendering process.
Similarly, a layer of noise, usually comprising circles but occasionally rectangles, is slowly formed as the piece progresses. This is a separate layer to the main render, so it always remains as an overlaid detail. It's subtle, but necessary for texture and variety.

Watching a piece render is not necessarily an unpleasant experience, but the early parts of the render are harsh and sudden. Subtletly comes later, as the piece builds. As a compromise between totally hiding the render process and focusing on the later aspects, I fade the piece into view as the render proceeds. I have a soft spot for unusual horror-related quotes, so a render progress bar and a little pretention have found their way into the piece.
Additionally, a detailed description of the render process and parameters is shown as the piece loads. This can be hidden with 'i', and if the viewer has not interacted with the piece by the time rendering is completed, the information is removed to reveal the full piece.

9614.d:
“The tinnitus like silence tearing the eardrums; a glare of darkness burned into the retina. “


As a visual & sound designer, my routine job is more related to new media installations, interactive programming design and lighting design. Explore to different luminaries and light sources, I gradually discover the relationship between light and sound waves. The role of reverberations are often sculptured the space when processing sounds, just like the lights play a similar role in 3D worlds. Reflections in the space make the sound more realistic, while the presence of light emphasis the dimensionality and depth of the space as well.

These scenes made of light and time remind me the painting and sculptures in the early 20th century, Futurism, which is characterized by technology, speed and violence. Umberto Boccioni and Gino Severini for instance. Nowadays, when we are free to deal with digital art beyond the existence of print or various archival forms, will it be an art movement called meta-futurism? Perhaps only things beyond our imagination can be called the future.

The project has been described during testing as being like picking up a camera that has fallen into space. It could be a collection of extreme brightness or endless darkness. If you decide to go into the space,  a carefully risk assessment is necessary.


Controls:

Click -> activate rotate control. (swipe gesture on mobile device)

Esc -> exit rotate and restart the rendering. (one tap on mobile device)

(Explore your own world by clicking on the canvas and rotate the viewpoint, tap “esc” to see the new result.)

The code used to calculate path tracing environment is from the three.js-PathTracing-Renderer ([https://github.com/erichlof/THREE.js-PathTracing-Renderer](https://github.com/erichlof/THREE.js-PathTracing-Renderer)), created by Erich Loftis.

Three directional lights (Red, Green and Blue) are aimed to a canvas filled with randomly positioned blocks. Each light brightens the canvas and projects shadows behind each block. Other three colors (Yellow, Magenta and Cyan) emerge because of the additive property of light.

This process creates an illusion that tricks the eye into seeing the full color spectrum. On some occasions it's very bright like rainbows, and sometimes it takes beautiful pastel notes. The line patterns crossing each other will also reveal new textures and shapes. It can look like glitches (old TV noise is the first thing that comes to mind) or it can take a more organic form like complex waves.

Minting this piece allows you to get it as a physical print if you choose to. More information below

-Grid type: Complete (30%), Lines and dots (30%), Lines (30%), Dots (10%)

Export: 
Click on open live then : 
-Press “J” to save as a high resolution JPG. 
-Press “S” to save as SVG  (the export takes some time)

Physical print : 

If you own this token, you are entitled to get a physical print made with my trusty pen plotter, and signed with my regular human hand ;). It’s drawn using sakura gelly roll pens on A3 paper (Fabriano black / Daler rowney white ).
It comes at an extra cost of 40XTZ (unless you have minted an edition with the free print feature set to “yes”). You can find the form to claim your physical copy here: https://fabax.art/blogs/infos/pattern-grid-chaos-nft

This PFP project was born from a core idea I was drawn into for many years. answering the question "what do I want my art to be about?" or "what ideas do I need to express in my art" . and my answer was "The contradictions and the contrasts". and mostly the contradiction I always found in beauty and perfection or better say in "KITSCH" 
"  kitsch is the absolute denial of shit, in both literal and figurative senses of the word; kitsch excludes everything from its purview which is essentially unacceptable in human existence." Milan Kundera writes .a kitsch can be many things , it can be a political idea, a video game , the idea of how our parents know everything or maybe a doll made specifically to look perfect. these kind of perfections shatter as we keep going on and this feeling, the feeling of a shattered kitsch is what I explore in my art and what I tried to put into this pfp project. these broken dolls come with an ironic dialogue to help you imagine their stories . This whole pfp is about the irony in shattered perfection. also they're kinda cute too ;) Enjoy! 

Art by No One Noise 
Codes by ArtaNik
special thanks to these people for translations : 
Bahar, Maryam, Mehrsa, Parisa, Dan and Kozy

9668.d:
specture:::numbat

generative numbats (pointy lines) searching for termites (Langton's ants scaled down, on other planes) to eat on the blockchain. chaos ensues

:::

the numbat is a marsupial that is extinct in my state of NSW, Australia, and is endangered in other parts of the country. it is effectively an ant-eater (also known as Noombat, Walpurti, Banded Ant-eater), obsessed with termites, so much so, they reset their body clock to wake when the termites are active during the day, and live in hollow trees/logs of the Eucalypt woodlands. they have long tongues and pointy snouts and strong paws to dig out termites in their 'galleries' — shallow tunnels and pathways between termite mounds.

:::

this work uses morphogenetic algorithms/methods to represent the key behaviours and characteristics of the species once they've been uploaded to the blockchain, rather than a realistic representation:
 
- Langton's Ant algorithm to represent the termites and their galleries — code is based on Daniel Shiffman / The Coding Train's Langton's Ant example code (MIT licence), then modified, and scaled

- elongated physical characteristics for the numbats — pointy lines to represent their snouts and long thin tongues

- multiple planes, thickness & colour of lines influenced by Iakov Georgievich Chernikhov (1889–1951), to free [architecture] from the ground and create a new order

- this is a 3D WEBGL work — the 3D text blocks ('hash' as text) are usually found on a hidden plane represent the environment of the blockchain

- this work continues the specture series - putting endangered/extinct/imaginary species onto the blockchain


WEBGL
previews & fullscreen mode may differ from the main work

9687.d:
Instructures explores the endless and diverse outcomes when a minimal and straightforward set of instructions are followed to build structures out of cubes. Between 4 and 8 instructions are selected and used to generate a unique structure for each edition. The available instructions are “stack”, “pile”, “plane” and “sculpt”. As a last step, flat and/or rounded corner details are optionally added to each structure.

Each artwork includes the set of instructions that were followed to build the structure. These instructions can be followed to build new structures using other methods in addition to programming, e.g. sculpting, printing, drawing, painting etc., and I plan on using this body of work to do exactly that. This project is, in fact, the result of an algorithm initially developed to generate interesting compositions and structures out of cubes to be used as points of departure for drawings, prints and paintings.

Even though the algorithm is focused on generating unique structures, the additional variations in scale, composition, colour, viewing angle and drawing style create an even wider array of generative outcomes. Some outputs are recognisable as three-dimensional orthographic drawings while others are more abstract. Instructures attempts to strike a balance between traditional art and the more technical nature of computer and blockchain art by blending visual cues from both disciplines. My hope is that the works can be appreciated by audiences from both of these worlds.

“The idea becomes a machine that makes the art.” — Sol Lewitt

=======
Each artwork is interactive allowing the viewer to rotate, move and zoom in on the structure.

[A] Move left

[<] Rotate clockwise
[>] Rotate anti-clockwise

Original artwork by Herman Pretorius, 2022

9693.d:
"VADFAD : 1Gen" is an experimental generative art piece that attempts to highlight some of the inherent contradictions surrounding the discussion of non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and its place as a vehicle for artistic creation, artistic expression and the potential of remuneration for artists.

s - Screenshot (PNG)

g - Download SVG

To the extent possible, the source code is dedicated to the public domain (CC0) and can be used for any purpose, even commercial, by anyone. All third party libraries used are libre/free. Please check individual files for their respective licenses.

The hope is that the "VADFAD : 1Gen" NFT draws a parallel to other technological trends of the past and highlights how new technologies that are only just being understood, or experimented with, can have unforeseen benefits and whose enjoyment might seem obscure to an outside observer.

The video game arcade industry helped create video game empires, drive the adoption of home video consoles and advance the proliferation of personal computers. Just as video games of the past helped promote innovative new technologies, NFTs have the potential to drive innovation in other markets that aren't well understood or explored yet.

By combing a 1980s "8-bit" aesthetic, "VADFAD : 1Gen" tries to touch on the nostalgia for the arcade video game era of the 1980s while using a generative process to create almost surely unique 8-bit like monster creations. The combination of styles is done to try emphasize the similarity between the two eras, where the exuberance for the new technology, art and entertainment of the past has a similar spirit to the exhilaration of the present.

"VADFAD : 1Gen" is a continuation of "VADFAD" incorporating different compositions, color palettes and export options.

This work hopes to add to the conversation about examining the reality of the ecosystem that we've developed around digital goods and intellectual property.

This work takes inspiration from the artist `Jared Tarbel`.

9701.d:
Harlequins

---

WebGL2, a fast GPU will make it more enjoyable. There's an initial pre-compute phase for the animation and that can pause a slow GPU for a few seconds.

---

Harlequins is an exploration in generating beautiful color and texture out of often-discordant beginnings. Much like our world.

Each Harlequin has random materials, background, and a random number of moons around it. Each frame adds more painted light and turns the initial harsh scene into a dreamlike blending of color, creating smooth matte colors on the central orb.

Harlequins is the result of a few months of generative work and lookdev on top of older long-exposure path tracing shaders. The runner and custom WebGL lib are written in TypeScript, lot of GLSL for the fragment shaders, then the whole thing is compiled, minified, and inlined into the final single self-contained HTML file. 6.4k zipped.


Ilmari Heikkinen 2022. Have fun.

---

Press space to enter the display mode. The display mode generates infinite new variants of your minted scene, displaying each one for a short while. Great for chilling out for a bit.

Press s to take a screenshot.

Double-click to render a new variant.

[Paolo Curtoni is a member of the "Colorless Green Ideas" collective, a laboratory aimed at exploring the relation between art, language and meaning. www.colorless-green-ideas.io]

"Stream of Consciousness: narrative technique intended to render the flow of myriad impressions - visual, auditory, physical, associative, and subliminal - that impinge on the consciousness of an individual and form part of his awareness along with the trend of his rational thoughts. [...]" (from Encyclopædia Britannica)

Now imagine this process, this stream of thoughts brought to the level of a social mind, of an entire community or society. The expression of a collective consciousness. Sixty-seven million stories of personal experiences, told spontaneously, without inhibitions, in the shelter of the anonymity of a social network (Experience Project, now discontinued): this is the enormous collection of human thoughts that has been used to synthesize an artificial mind, in some way representative of an entire generation of people.

Using language technologies, the whole collection of millions stories has been linguistically analysed and distilled into a semantic model using Deep Learning techniques, in order to create this artificial mind, the actionable knowledge behind the social network.

Each word is linked to the previous one by a semantic similarity, computed with the AI model. As a result, the words are interconnected by an evolving semantic coherence, like a loose interior monologue of this collective mind. 9735.d:
Cellular automaton forming ever-evolving chipset structures. Watch the automaton construct increasingly complex connections and paths until it become unrecognizable from mere noise.

This piece is based on a variation of a cyclic cellular automata (CCA).
CCA's are systems in which each cell may only increase its state if a certain number of neighbor cells have a state-value exactly one higher than itself. The number of possible states can be arbitrarily defined. Moreover, the states are modular, meaning cells cycle back to the first state after reaching the highest possible state. 

In this variation, there are four automata running simultaneously across the whole grid. Each automaton has its own ruleset and number of states causing different behaviors. However, the rulesets can also influence each other, allowing even more complex behavior to emerge. These rulesets are more diverse than in traditional CCAs, in that different state changes are allowed to occur if the number of neighbors with a higher state exceeds a certain threshold. Additionally, state changes are not restricted to be simple incrementations, but also allow operations such as substracting, multiplying and division. Values may be any of the other state values of the cell itself or its neighbors. 

This allows extremely complex behavior to emerge but also means that this automaton was very difficult to tame and to produce any aesthetically pleasing results. 

This iteration was achieved by using a genetic algorithm with myself being the judge of fitness, to continuously mutate and improve on past iterations. After analyzing 100s of different rulesets, I found this variation. What followed was (a lot) of fine-tuning by hand until reaching this final product. 

Code: https://github.com/Bewelge/CCA-WebGL
Preview with settings: https://bewelge.github.io/CCA-WebGL/

7 different color palettes. 

Controls:
Space - Pause/Unpause
Up/down - Increase/Decrease blending
S - Download image
F - Fill window
R - Raw shader output
D - Restart automaton
N - Restart with new starting pattern

Created in Javascript with Three.js

Requires WebGL and a decent device to run. Please check that it runs on your device before minting.
